ocf.text: Our cash flows are comprised of three primary classifications: cash flows from operating activities, cash flows from investing activities, and cash flows from financing activities. The decrease in cash and cash equivalents was due to operating activities using $32,000 of cash, investing activities using $186,000 of cash, and financing activities using $4.6 million of cash. Operating activities decreased primarily due to fluctuations in operating assets and liabilities and non-cash operating changes in account balances. Investing activities decreased cash by $186,000 as a result of the net change in loans receivable. Financing activities used $3.4 million of cash to fund deposit outflows, $1.4 million in refunds of stock subscriptions and $137,000 in stock issuances costs paid, which amounts were partially offset by $186,000 of proceeds from stock subscription conversion deposits and a $166,000 increase in advances from borrowers for insurance and taxes. The $4.9 million reduction in cash and cash equivalents during the three months ended March 31, 2025 to $5.1 million contributed to the reduction in total assets to $37.9 million from $44.0 million at December31, 2024.

prov.text: Provision for Credit Losses. We made no provision for credit losses in either the three months ended September 30, 2026 or 2025. Our total non-performing assets as of September 30, 2026 and 2025 were $152,000 and $72,000, respectively. The allowance for credit losses was $185,000 at September 30, 2026, representing 122% of non-performing assets at September 30, 2026. As of September 30, 2026, we had three loans totaling $152,000 that were on nonaccrual. No additional provision for credit losses was deemed necessary in the loan portfolio.

nonint.text: Noninterest Expense . Noninterest expense increased by $2,000, or 0.5%, to $402,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $400,000 for the comparable period of 2025. The increase in noninterest expense was due to an increase of $14,000 or 6.7% in salary and employee benefit expenses, partially offset by a reduction in general insurance of $10,000 and advertising expenses of $2,000.

nonop.text: Interest Expense . Total interest expense increased by $1,000 or 2.1% to $48,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $47,000 the comparable period of 2025. The increase was due to the increase in the average balance of certificates of deposit during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 2025, offset in part by the reduction in the average rate paid between the periods as we continued to elect not to renew higher rate certificates that matured during the period. The average balance of certificates of deposit increased during the three months ended September 30, 2026, by $270,000, while the average rate paid declined 13 basis points, from 3.03% for the three months ended September 30, 2025, to 2.90% in the three months ended September 30, 2026.

Net interest income.text: Our results of operations depend primarily on our net interest income. Net interest income is the difference between the interest income we earn on our interest-earning assets and the interest we pay on our interest-bearing liabilities. Our results of operations are also affected by our provisions for credit losses, noninterest income and noninterest expense. Noninterest income consists primarily of rental income and service charges and other fees on deposit accounts. Noninterest expense consists primarily of expenses related to salaries and employee benefits, occupancy and equipment, data processing, audit and regulatory examination fees, insurance premiums, and other expenses.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest Income . Noninterest income decreased $2,000, or 22%, to $7,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026. Noninterest income is comprised of customer service charges and rental income.

intro.text: Magnolia Bancorp, Inc. (“Magnolia Bancorp” or the “Company”) was incorporated by Mutual Savings and Loan Association (“Mutual Savings” or the “Association”) in May 2024 as part of the conversion of Mutual Savings from the mutual to the stock form of organization (the “Conversion”). The Conversion was completed on January 14, 2025, at which time the Company acquired all of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of the Association and the Association became a wholly owned subsidiary of Magnolia Bancorp. Concurrently with consummation of the Conversion, the Company completed its initial public offering and issued 833,750 shares of its common stock for an aggregate of $8.3 million. Total net proceeds from the offering were approximately $6.9 million (including shares issued to the Company’s employee stock ownership plan (“ESOP”)).

s.t: The Company’s cash flow depends on earnings from the investment of the net proceeds from the stock offering that it retains, and any dividends received from Mutual Savings and Loan Association.
Deposits have traditionally been our primary source of funds for use in lending activities.
We rely upon personalized customer service, long-standing relationships with customers, and our favorable reputation in the community to attract and retain local deposits.
An institution’s assessment rate depends upon the perceived risk of the institution to the Deposit Insurance Fund, with institutions deemed less risky paying lower rates.
Our primary sources of funds are deposits, principal and interest payments on loans, and to a lesser extent borrowings.
The levels of these assets depend on our operating, financing and lending activities during any given period.
